Alright, I've just finished writing a substantial portion of the client-side codebase. The sequence so far has been:

1. Created the basic HTML skeleton (index.html).
2. Added the main stylesheet (site.css) with the theme variables and layout basics.
3. Implemented the API helper module (api.js) for server communication and state handling.
4. Added the 2D avatar rendering utilities (avatar2d.js) for procedural faces.
5. Started the 3D engine by adding the world builder (engine/world.js) and the physics controller (engine/physics.js).
6. Completed the player character module (engine/player.js) that builds a blocky avatar using three.js meshes and canvas‑generated textures.

Each of these files compiled without errors (the tool calls all reported successful creation). The repository now contains the core building blocks: a UI layer, networking helpers, 2D avatar drawing, and the foundational 3D engine (scene setup, physics, player mesh). 

What’s missing to have a minimally functional game client? Looking at the typical architecture for a Roblox‑style web game, after the engine core we still need:

- An audio subsystem: the game uses synthesized sound effects (jump, collect, hit, etc.). A small SFX synth module will let us play these cues without loading external audio files, keeping the “no assets” philosophy.
- The main client entry point: this will wire together networking (WebSocket or fetch polling), camera controls, HUD elements (health, inventory, score), chat UI, and the various game modes (play, lobby, spectate). This file will import the engine modules we just wrote, set up the render loop, and handle user input.

The user (or the project description) has been asking for the full client stack, and I've already announced each major chunk as I completed it. The pattern in my previous messages was to state what component was just added, e.g., “Now client shared helpers…”, “Now 3D engine: world builder, physics, character.” Following that pattern, after finishing the engine core I should inform the user that the next steps are the SFX synth and the overall game client.

Therefore, the appropriate next response is a concise status update that signals completion of the engine core and announces the upcoming modules: the sound effects synthesizer and the client (networking, camera, HUD, chat, modes). This keeps the user informed and sets expectations for the next code files I’ll generate.

Thus I will output a short message: “Engine core done. Now SFX synth + the game client (networking, camera, HUD, chat, modes).”

content.text: Engine core done. Now SFX synth + the game client (networking, camera, HUD, chat, modes).
